Hence Option C is correct.

The painting illustrates the popular Rajasthani desert folk romance of Dhola and Maru. In this vivid folio from a Ragamala series, prince Dhola and princess Maru are depicted eloping on the back of a magnificently caparisoned royal camel racing across the desert. Two male attendants bearing swords and shields run alongside on foot, accompanied by a loyal hunting hound leading the way. questionText:
Arrange the evolutionary stages of Kishangarh and Jaipur art in chronological sequence:
(A) Amer school court portraits and Ragamala suites under Mirza Raja Jai Singh
(B) Establishment of the Suratkhana (painting department) in the new planned city of Jaipur
(C) Nihal Chand paints the spiritualized portrait of Radha (Bani Thani) at Kishangarh (c. 1750 A.D.)
(D) Guman paints the epic Ramayana masterpiece 'Bharat Meets Rama at Chitrakuta' (mid-to-late 18th c.)

Amer court art preceded the founding of Jaipur's Suratkhana, while Nihal Chand's mid-18th c. Kishangarh zenith coincided with Guman's mature Jaipur narrative works.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.
